The hospital has relied on a mobile MRI available two days a week and recently began construction to bring permanent MRI capabilities to the medical center, giving patients greater access to imaging when they need it.The medical center is also preparing to offer chemotherapy locally for the first time.
 
The medical center is also preparing to offer chemotherapy locally for the first time.  

"It's close to my heart. I think it would be a great service," Waldbillig said.  

For patients, expanding these services can mean fewer trips out of town and more opportunities to receive care close to home. They also illustrate the kinds of investments rural healthcare providers across North Dakota are making and the types of needs RHTP can help communities address. 

Through RHTP, North Dakota Health and Human Services is partnering with rural communities to strengthen local healthcare and improve access to services closer to home. The program supports innovative projects that help communities meet local needs, whether that's expanding technology, improving care coordination or adding services that previously required patients to travel long distances. 

These are the kinds of innovations North Dakota recently had the opportunity to showcase to representatives from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). During their visit to North Dakota, CMS met with providers and partners to learn more about the unique realities of delivering healthcare in rural communities and how the Rural Health Transformation Program is helping address those challenges. 

"If there's a way that we can harness funds to be able to get specialty services here locally, to be able to get technology here locally, to keep individuals, that helps us be sustainable in the future," Waldbillig said. 

For rural communities, success isn't measured only by new equipment or expanded services. It's measured by whether people can stay in their hometowns to receive quality care, whether providers can continue serving their neighbors and whether communities remain strong and healthy for generations to come. 

"Local people have got to be able to say, 'I want to go there. They provide great care. I want to stay,'" Waldbillig said.  

Because when people can get the care they need close to home, the benefits extend beyond the hospital walls.

In the Fargo, North Dakota area and Duluth, Minnesota area, you may work with a special patient navigator who helps you manage oral chemotherapy medicine and its side effects.

### Oral Chemotherapy

In the Fargo, North Dakota area and Duluth, Minnesota area, you may work with a special patient navigator who helps you manage oral chemotherapy medicine and its side effects. You’ll learn about:

  * Oral Cancer Medicines
  * Safety tips for using oral chemotherapy at home
  * When to call your care team about side effects
  * Financial information and programs

### Intrathecal Chemotherapy

If cancer affects your central nervous system, you may get intrathecal chemotherapy. This approach delivers medicine through a spinal tap or under your scalp.

## Immunotherapy

Immunotherapy, also called biotherapy, uses medicines to make your body’s natural defenses fight cancer. Some types of immunotherapy are targeted therapies. That means they focus on cancer-related cells and leave healthy cells alone.

You’ll notice fewer side effects with immunotherapy than with chemotherapy. You may get immunotherapy as part of a care plan that also includes chemotherapy or radiation.

Your doctor might recommend a checkpoint inhibitor, a type of immunotherapy that lets your immune system respond more strongly than usual. This treatment may help you if you have:

  * Advanced bladder cancer
  * Head and neck cancer
  * Hodgkin’s lymphoma
  * Kidney cancer
  * Metastatic melanoma
  * Non-small cell lung cancer

## Specialty Pharmacy

Find some cancer medicines through Essentia Health-Specialty Pharmacy. Choose to pick up your prescription drugs or receive them by mail or delivery service.
